neighbours.label: ' over' right after roll/rolled/rolling (the phrasal verb 'roll over'), literal or figurative (crushing an opponent)
fire: When the vet touched her belly, the old dog rolled over and waited for more scratches.
The car hit black ice, skidded off the highway and rolled over twice before stopping.
Our team rolled over the visitors in the second half, winning by thirty points.
Every morning the baby tries to roll over on the mat, giggling the whole time.
The kayak suddenly rolled over in the rapids, and Jake had to swim to shore.
Critics accused the senator of rolling over whenever the party leadership made demands.
After the alarm rang, Tom just rolled over and went back to sleep for another hour.
In the cup final the champions rolled over a tired opponent without breaking a sweat.

The truck skidded on the wet road and slammed into a fence near the farm.
Our team beat the visitors comfortably, scoring four goals in the second half.

The meeting is over, so everyone can head home early tonight.

The ball rolled slowly across the green and stopped short of the hole.
